requirements.text: Every MUST or MUST NOT requirement on documents or hosts in an HCS document MUST be referenced by at least one conformance case that satisfies it and at least one conformance case that violates it.
A conformance case MUST NOT reference a requirement identifier that does not exist in `requirements/requirements.json`.
A host MUST NOT reject a document because it contains extension members it does not understand.
An extension member MUST NOT change the validity verdict a host reaches for the members defined by HCS.
A catalog manifest MUST validate against the HCS-0001 catalog manifest schema for the `hcsVersion` it declares.
A host MUST read `hcsVersion` before any other validation and MUST report `unsupported_hcs_version`, not `manifest_invalid`, when it does not implement that contract.
Entry `id` values MUST be unique within a catalog manifest; a host MUST report `duplicate_entry` for every repeated id.
`contentHash` MUST be `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits or `sha512:` followed by 128 lowercase hex digits.
A contribution `path` MUST be relative, use `/` as separator, and MUST NOT contain a `..` segment.
A contribution `kind` MUST be `skill`, `mcp-server` or an extension name.
Every entry MUST declare `mediaType`.
A host MUST verify that fetched package bytes have exactly `size` bytes and match `contentHash` before unpacking or executing any of them, and MUST report `integrity_mismatch` otherwise.
A host MUST NOT activate an entry that has a contribution whose `kind` it does not implement, and MUST report `unsupported_contribution` for that entry.
When `compatibility.platforms` is present, a host MUST NOT activate the entry unless one item matches the host platform, and MUST report `platform_incompatible` otherwise.
A host MUST validate a catalog manifest without executing code from any package.
When `compatibility.hosts` is present, a host MUST NOT activate the entry unless one item names the host's id and lists the host's version exactly, and MUST report `version_incompatible` otherwise.
A host MUST be able to unpack packages of media type `application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+gzip` as described in section 3.4.
A host MUST NOT activate an entry whose `mediaType` it does not implement, and MUST report `unsupported_contribution` for that entry.
A producer SHOULD build package archives deterministically, so that `contentHash` changes only when the packaged content changes.

A host SHOULD reject a document that exceeds its declared maximum size or maximum nesting depth with `manifest_invalid` before schema validation, and SHOULD declare limits of at least 4 MiB (4 194 304 bytes) and 64 levels.
A capability reference in an HCS document MUST match the capability reference grammar.
A host MUST match a required capability to providers by capability reference only, never by the id of the package that provides it.
A host MUST treat two references with the same capability id and different majors as different contracts.
The owner of a contract SHOULD use a capability id whose leading segments are a reversed domain name it controls.
The owner of a contract SHOULD publish a new major when a change can break an existing provider or consumer.
A host MUST resolve a catalog without executing code from any package.
A host MUST report `missing_dependency` for an entry when no other eligible entry and no host built-in provides a capability id it requires.
A host MUST report `version_incompatible`, not `missing_dependency`, when the required capability id is provided only at other majors.
A host MUST report `ambiguous_provider` when more than one provider matches a required reference, and MUST NOT choose one of them implicitly.
A host MUST fail an entry whose requirement was satisfiable only by entries that themselves failed, reporting `missing_dependency` for it.
A host MUST report `dependency_cycle` for every entry whose requirements form a cycle, and MUST NOT activate any of them.
A host MUST place every entry after all the entries that provide its requirements in the activation order, and MUST break ties by ascending entry id compared as byte strings.
A host MUST apply one declared activation policy, `all-or-nothing` or `partial`, to every desired-set transition.
A host whose activation policy is `all-or-nothing` MUST NOT select any entry of a new desired set when resolution reported an error for that set, and MUST keep the previous desired set active.
A host whose activation policy is `partial` MUST select exactly the entries in the activation order.
A host MUST NOT run code from a package before its entry reaches `prepared`.
A host that reports entry state MUST use the state names in section 2 and the HCS-0004 status schema.
When a host moves from one desired set to another and any entry selected for activation fails to reach `active`, the host MUST return every entry to the state it had before the transition began.
A host MUST stop entries in the reverse of their activation order.
A host MUST report `unsupported_capability` for a call to a capability whose providing entry is not `active`.
A host MUST NOT dispatch new calls to an entry in `draining`.
A host that abandons a lifecycle step because it exceeded the host's deadline MUST move the entry to `failed` with code `timeout`.
A host MUST deny an operation that needs a permission unless it holds a grant for that entry and that permission, and MUST report the denial with code `permission_denied`.
A host MUST NOT treat a permission request, or any contribution metadata such as Agent Skills `allowed-tools`, as a grant.
A host MUST evaluate grants when each operation is dispatched, so that a revoked grant denies every operation dispatched after the revocation.
A host MUST NOT let an extension member on a request turn the request into a grant.
An error a host reports for an HCS-defined failure MUST validate against the HCS-0006 error schema.
A host MUST NOT report a `code` outside the closed set in section 3; distribution-specific detail goes in `details` under extension members.
When an HCS error is carried in a JSON-RPC 2.0 error response, the HCS error object MUST be the value of `error.data.hcsError`.
When an HCS error is carried as an RFC 9457 problem details object, its `type` MUST be `urn:hcs:error:<code>`, where `<code>` equals `hcsError.code`.
When an HCS error is carried as an RFC 9457 problem details object, the HCS error object MUST be the value of the extension member `hcsError`.

A host MUST check an envelope's `hcsVersion` and then its shape against the HCS-0007 envelope schema before verifying any signature, reporting `unsupported_hcs_version` or `manifest_invalid` as HCS-0001-R002 and HCS-0001-R001 do for catalogs.
A key set MUST validate against the HCS-0007 key set schema and MUST NOT list two keys with the same `keyid`; a host MUST report `manifest_invalid` otherwise.

The signature input of an envelope or key set MUST be the DSSE v1 pre-authentication encoding of its payload type and of the RFC 8785 serialization of the document without its `signatures` member, as defined in section 4.
An envelope or key set MUST NOT contain a number that is not an integer between -(2^53-1) and 2^53-1.

A host MUST NOT accept an envelope unless valid signatures from at least `threshold` distinct public keys of its accepted key set, each within its validity window, cover the signature input, and MUST report `signature_invalid` otherwise.
A host MUST NOT accept an envelope whose `binding` is not exactly equal to the host's assignment (same member names, same values), and MUST report `permission_denied` otherwise.
A host MUST NOT accept an envelope when the current time is equal to or later than `expires`, and MUST report `signature_invalid` otherwise.
A host MUST NOT accept an envelope whose `sequence` is lower than the last accepted one, or equal to it with different content, and MUST report `rollback_rejected` otherwise.
A host MUST apply the envelope checks in the order of section 5.2 and MUST report only the first check that fails.
A host MUST validate the enclosed catalog as HCS-0001 requires, after every envelope check has passed, and MUST NOT accept an envelope whose catalog fails that validation.

A host MUST NOT accept a key set unless valid signatures from at least the trust anchor's threshold of distinct root public keys cover its signature input, and MUST report `signature_invalid` otherwise.
A host MUST NOT accept a key set whose `version` is lower than the last accepted one, or equal to it with different content, and MUST report `rollback_rejected` otherwise.
A host MUST NOT accept a key set in which no key is within its validity window at the current time, and MUST report `signature_invalid` otherwise.
A host MUST count a signature toward a threshold only when the current time is equal to or later than its key's `notBefore` and earlier than its `notAfter`.

A host MUST record an envelope's `sequence` and content digest as accepted only after every check of section 5.2 has passed, and MUST keep the accepted state of envelopes and key sets across restarts.
A host that claims DISTRO-1 MUST use the `all-or-nothing` activation policy of HCS-0003.
A host MUST NOT modify the unpacked content of an active entry while moving to a new desired set; it MUST prepare the new set separately and switch to it as one step (HCS-0004-R003).
A host that runs a health check after starting a new desired set MUST treat a failed check as a failed transition under HCS-0004-R003 and return to the previous set.

A distribution SHOULD keep root private keys offline and SHOULD NOT hold any private key on the endpoint that serves envelopes and key sets, so that compromising that endpoint cannot produce an acceptable envelope.

A distribution SHOULD publish, for each package, SLSA Provenance v1 (`https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`) in an in-toto Statement v1 in a DSSE envelope signed by an online key of its key set, with a subject digest equal to the entry's `contentHash`.

A host that reports observed state to its distribution SHOULD send each report as a CloudEvents 1.0.2 event whose `data` is an HCS-0004 status document, and SHOULD carry errors over HTTP as RFC 9457 problem details as HCS-0006 section 4.2 defines.
